nodes.title: Algebraic presentation of the symplectic similitude group
nodes.statement: For g≥1 and a characteristic-zero field K, construct O_g(K)=K[x_ab,D,s,s⁻¹]/(D det(X)−1,ss⁻¹−1,(XJXᵀ−sJ)_ab), with 2g×2g X and J=[[0,I],[-I,0]]. Give it Δ(x_ab)=Σ_c x_ac⊗x_cb, Δ(s)=s⊗s, ε(X)=I, ε(s)=1 and matrix-inverse antipode. Its algebra maps to a commutative K-algebra A identify naturally with the matrix carrier of ArithmeticStatistics:ST.5/symplectic-similitude-group, and s evaluates to that node’s unique multiplier. Construct the quotient/presentation of that imported group, not another general definition of GSp.
hypotheses: g≥1; all coefficient fields have characteristic zero. Scalar extensions K/F are field extensions; BC_K denotes the Q-to-K specialization.
proofSteps: Use the existing GL determinant localization and adjoin an invertible scalar s. The relation XJXᵀ=sJ is stable under multiplication, identity and inverse, so the displayed ideal is a Hopf ideal.
Read off the natural points equivalence from the generators and relations; multiplier uniqueness uses a nonzero ±1 entry of J and g≥1.
The s=1 quotient is the pinned symplectic coordinate Hopf algebra. In rank one XJXᵀ=det(X)J, so eliminate s and recover the pinned GL₂ coordinate algebra.
acceptance: The multiplier-one fibre is Sp₂g, as a Hopf quotient, not just a set of Q-points.
For g=1 the multiplier is the determinant.

nodes.title: The integral central-similitude weight lattice
nodes.statement: Use X_g=Z×Z^g, with (m,u) representing t^m∏z_i^u_i. The multiplier weight is e_t=(1,0), z_i has weight e_i=(0,δ_i), and the second standard weight in pair i is e_t−e_i. The central scalar degree is d(m,u)=2m+Σu_i. Dominant weights are exactly u_1≥⋯≥u_g≥0, with m any integer; denote this subtype Dom_g. Pullback along (a,c)↦ca from Sp₂g×G_m sends (m,u) to (u,d), with image precisely d≡Σu_i (mod 2).
hypotheses: g≥1; all coefficient fields have characteristic zero. Scalar extensions K/F are field extensions; BC_K denotes the Q-to-K specialization.
proofSteps: Expand the diagonal character monomials: the torus coordinates t,z_i are independent invertible variables.
On scalar matrices z_i=c and t=c²; hence d=2m+Σu_i.
Simple roots e_i−e_(i+1) and 2e_g−e_t pair with coroots by u_i−u_(i+1) and u_g. Recover m=(d−Σu_i)/2 exactly when the parity condition holds.
acceptance: No positivity is imposed on m in Dom_g.
The central degree of the multiplier is 2 and of each standard weight is 1.

nodes.title: The diagonal GSp torus
nodes.statement: Construct the split torus T_g with character lattice X_g and diagonal immersion (t,z)↦diag(z_1,…,z_g,t/z_1,…,t/z_g). At Hopf level torusRestriction: O_g(K)→K[X_g] sends X to this diagonal matrix and s to [e_t]. Prove T_g is maximal, and fix the Borel whose positive simple roots are e_i−e_(i+1) and 2e_g−e_t. It restricts at t=1 to the pinned symplectic diagonal torus.
hypotheses: g≥1; all coefficient fields have characteristic zero. Scalar extensions K/F are field extensions; BC_K denotes the Q-to-K specialization.
proofSteps: The diagonal entries satisfy XJXᵀ=tJ, so the coordinate map descends and is a Hopf morphism. Its image contains t and every z_i and their inverses, proving closed immersion.

A matrix commuting with all independent diagonal torus characters is diagonal. The similitude equation then says its paired products are equal, so its centralizer is this torus, proving maximality through the generic split-pair interface. Compute the adjoint roots from the symplectic matrix entries and use the imported Sp Borel with the displayed positive roots. This proof does not use the subsequent central cover.
acceptance: The first and second basis vectors of pair i have torus weights e_i and e_t−e_i.
Set t=1 to recover diag(z_i,z_i⁻¹) in Sp.

nodes.title: Reciprocal Weyl action on the Laurent character algebra
nodes.statement: Let L_g=Z[X_g]=Z[t±1,z_1±1,…,z_g±1]. A permutation σ sends u_i to u_(σ⁻¹i), fixing m. The i-th reciprocal reflection sends (m,u) to (m+u_i,u with u_i replaced by −u_i); thus z_i↦t/z_i and t↦t. Extend these lattice automorphisms using MonoidAlgebra.domCongr. Their generator relations give W_g=(S_2)^g⋊S_g, canonically the Weyl group of (GSp,T). Define L_g^W as the Subring fixed by all these permutations and reflections.
hypotheses: g≥1; all coefficient fields have characteristic zero. Scalar extensions K/F are field extensions; BC_K denotes the Q-to-K specialization.
proofSteps: Define the explicit additive lattice automorphisms and use the pinned domain-congruence equivalence to act on the group algebra.

Check each reflection squares to identity, distinct reflections commute, and conjugation by σ relabels i. Normalizer representatives are the imported type-C symplectic permutation and pair-swap matrices; the multiplier central direction is fixed.
Define the fixed Subring by generator fixedness; the relations identify it with invariants for the semidirect Weyl group.
acceptance: A reflection fixes centralDegree and exchanges z_i with t/z_i.
An ordinary inversion z_i↦z_i⁻¹ with t fixed is not this Weyl action.

nodes.title: The central cover and its parity constraint
nodes.statement: For g≥1 in characteristic zero, (a,c)↦ca defines a faithfully flat central isogeny Sp₂g×G_m→GSp₂g with kernel μ₂ embedded by ε↦(εI,ε). Its pullback on diagonal character lattices is coverWeight. A rational representation of the product descends exactly when this diagonal μ₂ acts trivially. In particular the Sp highest weight u paired with scalar degree d descends iff d−Σu_i is even. GSp is split, connected and reductive, and the simple roots/coroots give Dom_g as above.
hypotheses: g≥1; all coefficient fields have characteristic zero. Scalar extensions K/F are field extensions; BC_K denotes the Q-to-K specialization.
proofSteps: Compute the multiplier of ca as c² and the kernel as (εI,ε), ε²=1. Adjoining a square root of an invertible multiplier gives a finite faithfully flat cover, so this is a quotient statement in the fppf topology, not surjectivity on Q-points.
Use the imported affine-group quotient/descent criterion and reductivity under central isogeny. The split torus and root calculation of CG.0 identify the lattice and dominant chamber.
On the Sp module of highest weight u, −I acts by (−1)^(Σu_i), while −1 in G_m acts by (−1)^d. Hence the kernel acts trivially exactly at the displayed parity.
acceptance: diag(I_g,2I_g) is a Q-point with multiplier 2 but has no lift to Sp(Q)×Q×; local fppf surjectivity remains valid.
Standard Sp weight requires odd scalar degree; ν has Sp weight 0 and scalar degree 2.

ReductiveGroups Layer 6 supplies semisimplicity, so its split relations also give the usual Grothendieck ring with exact-sequence relations. Evaluation on K-points gives a functor to abstract FDRep and a map to the existing TauCeti.repRing, without identifying these categories.

Use the pinned SplitK0 commutative-ring construction. Since GSp is connected reductive in characteristic zero, every short exact sequence splits by the requested semisimplicity result.

nodes.title: Rational models of the GSp highest-weight modules
nodes.statement: For λ=(m,u)∈Dom_g construct L_g,K(λ), an absolutely simple algebraic representation with that highest weight. Let a_k=u_k−u_(k+1)≥0, with u_(g+1)=0. First form the tensor product ∏_(k=1)^g P_k^⊗a_k, whose highest vector is rational and has highest weight (0,u), and take the comodule it generates. Then tensor with ν^m. The result has a one-dimensional highest line and scalar degree 2m+Σu_i.
hypotheses: g≥1; all coefficient fields have characteristic zero. Scalar extensions K/F are field extensions; BC_K denotes the Q-to-K specialization.
proofSteps: The explicit primitive highest vectors and the a_k give a rational highest tensor vector. Its generated subcomodule is the span of coefficient extractions from its coaction: restrict to the existing pinned matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra D, whose finite underlying module is supplied by matrixCoefficientSubcoalgebra_finite, and apply id⊗φ for φ∈D*. Coassociativity makes this span stable and minimal. The finite-dual and span constructions commute with flat field extension, so the rational generated component extends to the complex Cartan component.

After extension to C, apply imported semisimplicity to the tensor product and the highest-weight classification/uniqueness to its simple summands. The tensor highest vector is killed by positive-root operators and its weight u is the unique top weight, with a one-dimensional weight space. Its projection to a simple summand is either zero or a highest vector of weight u; uniqueness and the one-dimensional top line leave exactly one such summand. The generated submodule is therefore that simple Sp module: this proves the Cartan-component step here, rather than requesting it from the classification layer. The centre acts by Σu_i, and the central parity criterion descends the component to GSp.

Faithful extension proves simplicity and scalar endomorphisms over Q. The generic Hom base-change theorem makes End_K one-dimensional for every K/Q; semisimplicity over K therefore proves that each model remains simple. Twisting by ν^m gives every central-compatible highest weight, including negative m.
acceptance: The highest vector is constructed inside a tensor product; no assertion that an arbitrary complex module has a chosen rational form is substituted for the descent proof.

nodes.title: The positive reciprocal Laurent subring
nodes.statement: Define B_g as the Subring of L_g generated by all z_i and t/z_i, for g≥1; its Weyl-fixed subring is B_g^W=B_g∩L_g^W. Equivalently, a Laurent polynomial belongs to B_g iff every nonzero coefficient at (m,u) satisfies m+Σ_i min(u_i,0)≥0. This is a support condition on polynomials, not a positivity condition on their integer coefficients. Pure algebra defines this object independently of any representation category.
hypotheses: g≥1; all coefficient fields have characteristic zero. Scalar extensions K/F are field extensions; BC_K denotes the Q-to-K specialization.
proofSteps: Use the existing Subring.closure, not a second polynomial-ring foundation. Because g≥1, t=z_i(t/z_i) belongs to B_g.

A monomial in the generators has u_i=a_i−b_i and m=Σb_i, hence m+Σmin(u_i,0)=Σmin(a_i,b_i)≥0. Conversely choose b_i=max(−u_i,0), a_i=max(u_i,0), and multiply by t^(m−Σb_i), which has nonnegative exponent.

The support inequality is equivalently m+Σ_(i∈S)u_i≥0 for every subset S. These linear inequalities make it closed under addition of weights; the minimum functional itself is not additive. Integer sums and negatives preserve the allowed support.
acceptance: t belongs, but t⁻¹ does not. Integer coefficients may be negative.
At g=1 both z and t/z belong, whereas z⁻¹ does not.

nodes.statement: Construct a Z-algebra equivalence Z[T,X_1,…,X_g]≃B_g^W sending T to t and X_k to F_k. Thus B_g^W=Z[t,F_1,…,F_g] with no t⁻¹. All these generators are algebraically independent over Z. Its inclusion into L_g^W agrees with the full invariant presentation after inverting T.

proofSteps: Normalize a flip orbit by making all u_i nonnegative. Its least t exponent is m+Σmin(u_i,0), hence is nonnegative in B_g. The orbit sum is t^a times a product, over nonzero u_i only, of z_i^u_i+(t/z_i)^u_i. The recurrence from the full invariant proof expresses it integrally in t and x_i.
Therefore invariants under pair swaps are exactly Z[t,x_1,…,x_g]. Apply the pinned symmetric-polynomial equivalence over Z[t] to get Z[t,e_1(x),…,e_g(x)].

The same integral triangular change e_k↔F_k used in the full invariant presentation never introduces a negative t exponent. Algebraic independence follows from the full presentation and the inclusion of Z[t] into Z[t±1].

nodes.title: The exact highest-weight criterion for tensor occurrence
nodes.statement: For λ=(m,u)∈Dom_g, L(λ) occurs in a tensor power V^⊗d iff m≥0. More precisely, it occurs in V^⊗d iff m≥0 and d=2m+Σu_i. Every torus weight of V^⊗d lies in the support cone of B_g. Thus ch(L(λ)) belongs to B_g whenever m≥0; ν⁻¹ is excluded despite being a rational algebraic representation.
hypotheses: g≥1; all coefficient fields have characteristic zero. Scalar extensions K/F are field extensions; BC_K denotes the Q-to-K specialization.
proofSteps: A tensor basis chooses either z_i or t/z_i in each factor. Write its counts as a_i,b_i≥0: m=Σb_i and u_i=a_i−b_i. For a dominant highest weight this forces m≥0; scalar matrices also force d=2m+Σu_i. All such weights obey the support-cone inequality.

For sufficiency write u=Σ_(k=1)^g a_k(1^k), with a_k=u_k−u_(k+1). The preceding rational Cartan-product construction realizes L(0,u) as a summand of the tensor product of the P_k^⊗a_k, hence of V^⊗Σu_i.
For m≥0 tensor with ν^m, a summand of V^⊗2m by the pairing split. Semisimplicity and the central degree fix the exact tensor degree. Subrepresentation weights give the positive-character conclusion.
acceptance: L(0,0) occurs in degree 0 only; GSp has no invariant vector in V^⊗2, while its ν constituent has degree 2.
For g=1, det^m Sym^u V occurs at degree 2m+u exactly for m≥0.

In characteristic zero, central isogenies preserve connected reductivity, and every finite-dimensional rational algebraic representation of a connected reductive group is semisimple, over the original field as well as its algebraic closure.

Dominant integral highest weights are u_1≥⋯≥u_g≥0, each simple has a one-dimensional highest line and lower weights in the positive-root order, and the centre acts through its highest weight.
